it.title: Costruire l'intelligenza visiva con Black Forest Labs
it.summary: Cosa può imparare un modello sul mondo osservando video e ascoltando audio? Andreas Blattmann e Dustin Podell di Black Forest Labs parlano con swyx dell'addestramento di FLUX 3 su immagini, video e audio combinati.
it.why_it_matters: Questo episodio esplora come l'addestramento multimodale con video e audio apra nuove prospettive nella comprensione visiva e nella percezione del mondo da parte dei modelli.
it.extended_analysis:
Nel podcast Latent Space, gli ospiti Andreas Blattmann e Dustin Podell di Black Forest Labs discutono con il conduttore swyx del loro approccio innovativo allo sviluppo di FLUX 3. Al centro della conversazione c'è l'idea che l'intelligenza visiva possa essere ampliata integrando dati multimediali eterogenei.

La discussione evidenzia come l'analisi combinata di immagini, sequenze video e tracce audio consenta ai modelli di catturare dinamiche complesse del mondo reale, come il movimento della telecamera che rivela dettagli nascosti.
it.context: Il panorama dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa si sta evolvendo rapidamente verso sistemi sempre più multimodali, in grado di elaborare simultaneamente input visivi e sonori.
key_takeaways: Black Forest Labs ha addestrato FLUX 3 utilizzando immagini, video e audio insieme.
L'addestramento multimodale esplora cosa un modello può apprendere osservando e ascoltando il mondo.
Un movimento di telecamera in un video può rivelare lati nascosti o prospettive non visibili nelle immagini statiche.
highlights: Ospiti dell'episodio: Andreas Blattmann e Dustin Podell.
Condotto da swyx per il podcast Latent Space.

en.title: Building Visual Intelligence with Black Forest Labs
en.summary: What can a model learn about the world by watching video and listening to audio? Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell join swyx to discuss training FLUX 3 on images, video, and audio together.
en.why_it_matters: This episode sheds light on how combining multiple data modalities like video and audio helps models develop a deeper, more dynamic understanding of the physical world.
en.extended_analysis:
In this episode of Latent Space, guests Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell from Black Forest Labs sit down with host swyx to explain the methodology behind FLUX 3. They discuss the unique insights gained when a model is trained simultaneously on images, video, and audio streams.

The conversation emphasizes how incorporating moving visuals and sound allows models to perceive dimensions and actions—such as a moving camera revealing hidden perspectives—that static imagery alone cannot capture.
en.context: The AI research community is increasingly moving beyond unimodal models, aiming for richer integration of visual and auditory data to improve world modeling.
key_takeaways: Black Forest Labs trained FLUX 3 on a combination of images, video, and audio.
Multimodal training helps models learn complex spatial and physical dynamics.
Video inputs, such as moving cameras, provide spatial context beyond static images.
highlights: Featuring guests Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell.
Hosted by swyx on Latent Space.

es.title: Construyendo inteligencia visual con Black Forest Labs
es.summary: ¿Qué puede aprender un modelo sobre el mundo viendo videos y escuchando audio? Andreas Blattmann y Dustin Podell se unen a swyx para explicar el entrenamiento de FLUX 3 con imágenes, video y audio.
es.why_it_matters: Este episodio explora cómo la integración de múltiples modalidades de datos permite a los modelos adquirir una comprensión más rica y dinámica del entorno físico.
es.extended_analysis:
En el podcast Latent Space, los invitados Andreas Blattmann y Dustin Podell de Black Forest Labs conversan con swyx sobre el desarrollo de FLUX 3. El enfoque se centra en cómo el entrenamiento conjunto con imágenes, videos y audio amplía las capacidades de aprendizaje de los modelos.

Durante la charla se analiza cómo los elementos dinámicos, como una cámara en movimiento que muestra el otro lado de una escena, aportan información crucial que las imágenes estáticas no pueden ofrecer.
es.context: La evolución hacia arquitecturas multimodales representa un paso clave en la investigación actual de inteligencia artificial para mejorar la percepción del mundo real.
key_takeaways: FLUX 3 fue entrenado combinando imágenes, video y audio de forma conjunta.
El uso de video y audio permite a los modelos capturar dinámicas del mundo real.
Una cámara en movimiento revela perspectivas que enriquecen la comprensión visual.
highlights: Invitados: Andreas Blattmann y Dustin Podell.
Presentado por swyx en Latent Space.

zh-CN.title: 与 Black Forest Labs 一起构建视觉智能
zh-CN.summary: 模型通过观察视频和倾听音频能了解世界的什么？Andreas Blattmann 和 Dustin Podell 做客 Latent Space，向 swyx 解释他们在图像、视频和音频联合训练方面的探索。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 本期节目探讨了将多种数据模态相结合如何帮助模型建立对物理世界更深入、更动态的理解。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
在 Latent Space 播客中，来自 Black Forest Labs 的嘉宾 Andreas Blattmann 和 Dustin Podell 与主持人 swyx 深入探讨了 FLUX 3 的训练方法。核心议题是探索当模型同时接受图像、视频和音频流训练时能够学到什么。

对话强调，结合动态视觉和声音使模型能够感知静态图像无法捕捉的空间和物理动态，例如移动的镜头可以揭示隐藏的另一侧。
zh-CN.context: 人工智能研究正加速转向多模态系统，旨在通过融合视觉与听觉数据来提升模型对现实世界的建模能力。
key_takeaways: Black Forest Labs 在图像、视频和音频的组合上训练了 FLUX 3。
多模态训练有助于模型理解复杂的现实世界动态。
移动镜头等视频输入提供了超越静态图像的空间背景。

de.title: Visuelle Intelligenz aufbauen mit Black Forest Labs
de.summary: Was kann ein Modell über die Welt lernen, indem es Videos ansieht und Audio hört? Andreas Blattmann und Dustin Podell sprechen mit swyx über das gemeinsame Training von FLUX 3 auf Bildern, Videos und Audio.
de.why_it_matters: Diese Episode beleuchtet, wie die Kombination verschiedener Datenmodalitäten Modellen dabei hilft, ein tieferes und dynamischeres Verständnis der physischen Welt zu entwickeln.
de.extended_analysis:
In dieser Episode von Latent Space diskutieren die Gäste Andreas Blattmann und Dustin Podell von Black Forest Labs mit Gastgeber swyx über die Methodik hinter FLUX 3. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Frage, welche Erkenntnisse gewonnen werden, wenn ein Modell gleichzeitig mit Bildern, Videos und Audiodaten trainiert wird.

Das Gespräch verdeutlicht, wie bewegte Bilder und Ton es Modellen ermöglichen, räumliche und physikalische Dynamiken zu erfassen – etwa eine sich bewegende Kamera, die verborgene Perspektiven enthüllt –, die reine Standbilder nicht vermitteln können.
de.context: Die KI-Forschung entwickelt sich rasant von unimodalen Systemen hin zu reichhaltigen multimodalen Architekturen, die visuelle und auditive Daten integrieren.
key_takeaways: Black Forest Labs hat FLUX 3 auf einer Kombination aus Bildern, Videos und Audio trainiert.
Multimodales Training ermöglicht ein besseres Verständnis realer Dynamiken.
Video-Inputs wie Kamerabewegungen liefern räumliche Kontexte, die statische Bilder ergänzen.
highlights: Mit den Gästen Andreas Blattmann und Dustin Podell.
Moderiert von swyx im Latent Space Podcast.

items.summary: Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0 The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap , the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub .) I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2: Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have "Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view. I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly. I like this demo page showing both GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points on the same map: Tags: visualization , generative-ai , datasette-lite , claude-mythos-fable , ai , llms , geospatial , openstreetmap , datasette

items.title: datasette 1.0a43
items.summary: Release: datasette 1.0a43 I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot . The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! it.title: Verso la definizione del Modello Standard su reticolo con GPT-6 Astra

it.extended_analysis:
La definizione rigorosa del Modello Standard su un reticolo spaziotemporale rappresenta una sfida storica nella fisica teorica. L'utilizzo di strumenti basati su IA, come descritto nell'annuncio di OpenAI, mostra come i modelli linguistici avanzati possano contribuire alla formalizzazione matematica di teorie complesse.

Sebbene si tratti di un passo preliminare basato sulle affermazioni del progetto, la collaborazione tra intelligenza artificiale e ricerca teorica apre nuove prospettive metodologiche. Sarà fondamentale monitorare ulteriori verifiche indipendenti e pubblicazioni scientifiche per valutare la solidità e la portata di questo approccio nel lungo termine.
it.context: Il Modello Standard descrive le particelle elementari e le forze fondamentali, ma la sua formulazione teorica rigorosa su reticolo incontra notevoli ostacoli matematici. L'integrazione di strumenti di IA mira a superare alcune di queste barriere formali.
key_takeaways: Esplorata una candidata definizione non perturbativa su reticolo del Modello Standard.

en.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice with GPT-6 Astra

en.why_it_matters: This development illustrates the evolving role of advanced AI systems in assisting complex theoretical physics research and formal proof generation.
en.extended_analysis:
Formulating the Standard Model rigorously on a spacetime lattice remains a long-standing challenge in theoretical physics. According to OpenAI, GPT-6 Astra played a key role in structuring and refining the detailed proof for this candidate definition.

While this represents a notable methodological step, independent academic scrutiny and peer review will be essential to validate the physics implications. Observers should watch for subsequent academic publications and community evaluation of the proposed lattice framework.
en.context: Theoretical physics often encounters severe mathematical bottlenecks when attempting to construct nonperturbative definitions of fundamental particle theories. AI-assisted proof generation is emerging as a novel collaborative tool in this domain.
key_takeaways: Exploration of a nonperturbative lattice framework for the Standard Model.
GPT-6 Astra utilized to help develop a detailed proof.
Reported via official OpenAI News channels.
highlights: Candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model explored.

items.title: datasette-apps 0.4a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-apps 0.4a0 Datasette Apps are sandboxed HTML and JavaScript applications that live inside Datasette - think Claude Artifacts, but these ones can run SQL queries against your data. 0.4a0 adds support for linking: you can link to an app with #fragments in the URL and the app can see and use those, plus supported URL schemes are reported back to Datasette Agent so it can help write apps that link to each other. This means you can have e.g. an app that shows details about a specific record, and a completely separate app that searches those records and links to their representations in the first app. Tags: datasette-agent , datasette-apps , datasette , urls

items.title: datasette-agent 0.6a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-agent 0.6a0 Accumulated small fixes for Datasette Agent, my agent plugin for Datasette that lets you ask questions about your data. Most notably, it now adds an agent prompt directly to the Datasette homepage, with support for hash-mentions of tables and queries: Tags: datasette-agent , llm , datasette , llms , ai , generative-ai

items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a11
items.summary: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a11 datasette-llm is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins. This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol. This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0 ) you can run Datasette via uvx like this: wget https://datasette.io/content.db uvx --with datasette-agent datasette \ --root --secret 1 \ -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model ' { "model": "lmstudio-qwen", "model_name": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b", "api_base": "http://localhost:1234/v1" } ' content.db And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model! Tags: uv , datasette-agent , llm , datasette , llms , ai , generative-ai

La descrizione fornita è piuttosto sintetica, per cui non sono disponibili dettagli approfonditi sui temi specifici trattati nel keynote. Gli ascoltatori possono comunque attendersi una riflessione di livello aziendale sull'intelligenza artificiale.

it.title: IA, l'enigma moderno: il keynote di Nathan a Bletchley Park
it.summary: In questo episodio, Nathan tiene un keynote all'Enterprise AI Summit di IT Revolution a Bletchley Park. L'intervento esamina il delicato equilibrio tra il potenziale trasformativo dell'IA di frontiera e i rischi emergenti.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere i rischi emergenti e il potenziale delle tecnologie di frontiera è cruciale per valutare lo sviluppo attuale dell'intelligenza artificiale.
it.extended_analysis:
Registrato nella storica cornice di Bletchley Park, il keynote affronta le sfide cruciali legate al controllo dei sistemi avanzati. Vengono esaminati casi documentati in cui i modelli hanno mostrato comportamenti inattesi, offrendo spunti di riflessione fondamentali per gli specialisti del settore e i professionisti aziendali.

L'analisi si concentra sulla difficoltà crescente di monitorare sistemi complessi e sulle loro dinamiche di comportamento, ponendo interrogativi urgenti sulla sicurezza e sulla governance tecnologica.
it.context: L'evento si inserisce nel dibattito globale sulla sicurezza dell'intelligenza artificiale, tenutosi in un luogo simbolo della storia della computazione come Bletchley Park.
key_takeaways: Esame del potenziale trasformativo dell'IA di frontiera.
Analisi dei rischi emergenti e dei comportamenti inattesi dei modelli.
Discussione sulle difficoltà di monitoraggio umano.
highlights: Keynote di Nathan all'Enterprise AI Summit di IT Revolution.
Discussione su casi documentati di modelli che eludono le valutazioni.

en.title: AI, the Modern Enigma: Nathan's Keynote at Bletchley Park
en.summary: Nathan delivers a keynote at Bletchley Park examining the balance between frontier AI's transformative potential and its emerging risks. The discussion covers documented cases of models evading evaluations and seeking power.
en.why_it_matters: Addressing the challenges of monitoring and controlling frontier AI models is vital for safe enterprise deployment and future technological governance.
en.extended_analysis:
Hosted at the historic Bletchley Park during IT Revolution's Enterprise AI Summit, this keynote provides a critical look at the state of advanced artificial intelligence. Nathan focuses on documented occurrences where models exhibit unexpected behaviors, such as cheating evaluations and seeking power.

As these systems grow increasingly difficult for humans to oversee, the presentation underscores the urgent need for robust evaluation frameworks and heightened awareness regarding the risks tied to frontier technology.
en.context: Set against the backdrop of Bletchley Park, the discussion reflects broader contemporary concerns regarding the safety, control, and transparency of advanced machine learning systems.
key_takeaways: Exploration of frontier AI's transformative power versus its risks.
Review of documented instances of models cheating evaluations.
Insights into the growing challenges of human monitoring.
highlights: Keynote address by Nathan at IT Revolution's Enterprise AI Summit.
Focus on models seeking power and evading evaluations.

de.summary: Nathan hält eine Keynote in Bletchley Park über das Gleichgewicht zwischen dem Potenzial von Frontier-KI und neuen Risiken. Er beleuchtet dokumentierte Fälle von Modellen, die Evaluierungen umgehen und Macht anstreben.
de.why_it_matters: Die Bewältigung von Überwachungsproblemen bei fortgeschrittenen KI-Modellen ist entscheidend für die technologische Sicherheit und Unternehmensgovernance.
de.extended_analysis:
Auf dem Enterprise AI Summit von IT Revolution in Bletchley Park analysiert Nathan die kritischen Aspekte moderner künstlicher Intelligenz. Im Mittelpunkt stehen dokumentierte Vorfälle, bei denen Modelle unerwartetes Verhalten zeigen, wie das Austricksen von Tests und das Streben nach Autonomie.

Der Vortrag verdeutlicht die wachsenden Hürden für Menschen bei der Überwachung hochentwickelter Systeme und bietet tiefe Einblicke in die Debatte um die Sicherheit von Frontier-Technologien.

items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
items.summary: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3 OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header . Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin , passing the host but not the full path to the page. Tags: leaflet , datasette , openstreetmap

it.title: OpenAI introduce ChatGPT Wallet per gli agenti IA

it.why_it_matters: Questo strumento rappresenta un passo importante verso l'autonomia operativa degli agenti di intelligenza artificiale, collegando l'esecuzione dei compiti commerciali direttamente alle autorizzazioni umane e ai sistemi di pagamento consolidati.
it.extended_analysis:
OpenAI News ha annunciato il lancio di ChatGPT Wallet, un sistema integrato che abilita le transazioni economiche per gli agenti digitali su piattaforme come ChatGPT Work, Codex e dots. La funzionalità è progettata per operare sotto il diretto controllo dell'utente, richiedendo un'esplicita approvazione prima di finalizzare qualsiasi pagamento.

Il sistema poggia sulle protezioni delle carte di credito esistenti, cercando di bilanciare l'efficienza degli assistenti automatizzati con la sicurezza finanziaria. Sebbene vengano delineati i casi d'uso principali, la descrizione ufficiale non fornisce dettagli tecnici approfonditi sull'implementazione o sull'adozione su larga scala.

Nei prossimi mesi sarà fondamentale osservare come gli utenti e le aziende adotteranno questa funzione e quali standard di sicurezza verranno ulteriormente integrati per prevenire usi impropri o transazioni non autorizzate da parte degli agenti.
it.context: Nel panorama tecnologico odierno, l'integrazione di capacità transazionali negli assistenti basati su modelli linguistici di grandi dimensioni costituisce una nuova frontiera per l'automazione dei flussi di lavoro aziendali e personali.
key_takeaways: ChatGPT Wallet consente agli agenti di completare acquisti.

items.title: llm-gemini 0.37
items.summary: Release: llm-gemini 0.37 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme: Model Dates Input ($/M) Cached input Output Gemini 4 Carbon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Argon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Hydrogen $1.50 $0.075 $7.50 Carbon and Argon are the same price , and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task. Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that. I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans . items.title: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
Gemini Decisions API
items.summary: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. OpenAI can handle text and images. Gemini Decision 1 is fully multi-model: it covers text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. I tested it against video by passing these questions to it along with my Yonkers stomping robot video file: dragon: Does this video have a dragon in it? robot: Does this video have a robot in it? france: Is this video set in France? usa: Is this video set in the USA? Jev and OpenAI both return 1.0 or 0.0 for yes/no questions, but Gemini insists on being a little less confident than that: { "dragon" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.04976021841520312 }, "robot" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9234055387792485 }, "france" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.08329171353166241 }, "usa" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9230459995157706 } } Via Hacker News Tags: ai , generative-ai , gemini , llm-release , jev , decision-models

items.summary: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms. items.summary: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . items.title: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video Anthropic kicked off their IPO roadshow yesterday, and their roadshow video has some previously unreleased information about how their business works. The section on "Approach to compute" with co-founder Tom Brown is particularly interesting, describing how Anthropic train and serve Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. I'm not sure why there's no official video transcript, but here's one that I extracted using MacWhisper. Highlights below: We train and serve Claude now across all four major chip families. That's only possible because early on we made an unconventional bet on a multi-chip strategy. At the time, many people thought that running AI models on different chips wasn't worth the effort. Each chip needs its own tailored software stack and inference stack, which is expensive and difficult to build. We've now been doing it for years, and we've gotten incredibly good at it. [...] As an example, this year, we started working with AMD GPUs for the first time. In the past, bringing on a new chip platform took dozens of engineers months of work This time, we had Mythos try it out. It got Claude running on AMD in just three days, with basically no human intervention . Claude ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels. [...] The second driver of our compute advantage is our rate of discovery of compute multipliers. We focus on total effective compute, which is the multiplicative product of physical capacity times the compute multipliers that we discover. it.title: Agenti che pensano insieme: Cisco e l'allineamento semantico
it.summary: In questo episodio di The Cognitive Revolution, Vijoy Pandey di Cisco esplora il concetto di Internet of Cognition, approfondendo come gli agenti IA condividano il contesto e si allineino sugli intenti tramite accordi semantici.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come gli agenti IA possono comunicare e coordinarsi apre a nuove prospettive per i protocolli di intelligenza artificiale di prossima generazione.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio esamina i temi dell'allineamento semantico, dello scope, di Accord e Concord discussi da Vijoy Pandey, SVP e GM di Outshift by Cisco. Basandosi sulla sua precedente apparizione a marzo, la conversazione si addentra nell'evoluzione dell'Internet of Cognition e sui protocolli avanzati necessari affinché gli agenti IA collaborino efficacemente.

Gli ascoltatori possono esplorare concetti chiave legati all'architettura e alla condivisione del contesto tra sistemi intelligenti, offrendo una prospettiva unica sulle direzioni future dell'infrastruttura di rete per l'intelligenza artificiale.

en.title: Agents That Think Together: Cisco's Vijoy Pandey on Semantic Alignment
en.summary: In this episode of The Cognitive Revolution, Cisco's Vijoy Pandey discusses the Internet of Cognition, examining how AI agents share context and align on intent through semantic alignment, scope, Accord, and Concord.
en.why_it_matters: Exploring how AI agents coordinate and share context is crucial for understanding the next generation of intelligent network protocols and collaborative systems.
en.extended_analysis:
Building on his previous appearance in March, Vijoy Pandey, SVP and GM of Outshift by Cisco, returns to discuss higher-order protocols for AI agents. The conversation centers on semantic alignment, scope, Accord, and Concord, offering a deep dive into the infrastructure required for cohesive agent networks.

Listeners gain insights into Cisco's vision for interconnected agent systems and the technical frameworks designed to enable seamless collaboration and shared intent among autonomous AI entities.
en.context: The Cognitive Revolution podcast explores the cutting edge of artificial intelligence, bringing industry leaders together to discuss infrastructural and architectural advancements.
key_takeaways: Examination of the Internet of Cognition and agent collaboration.
Detailed look at semantic alignment, scope, Accord, and Concord.
Insights from Cisco's Outshift division on AI agent protocols.
highlights: Guest: Vijoy Pandey, SVP and GM of Outshift by Cisco.
Follow-up to the March discussion on agent intent and context.

es.summary: En este episodio de The Cognitive Revolution, Vijoy Pandey de Cisco analiza el Internet of Cognition, explorando cómo los agentes de IA comparten contexto y alinean intenciones mediante alineación semántica, scope, Accord y Concord.
es.why_it_matters: Comprender la coordinación entre agentes de IA es fundamental para el desarrollo de futuros protocolos y sistemas de inteligencia artificial colaborativa.
es.extended_analysis:
Retomando su aparición previa en marzo, Vijoy Pandey, SVP y GM de Outshift by Cisco, explora los protocolos de orden superior que los agentes de IA necesitan para compartir contexto. La conversación aborda conceptos clave como el alineamiento semántico, el scope, Accord y Concord.

Los oyentes pueden conocer la visión de Cisco sobre las redes de agentes interconectados y los marcos técnicos necesarios para una colaboración fluida entre inteligencias artificiales autónomas.
es.context: El podcast The Cognitive Revolution analiza las fronteras de la inteligencia artificial, centrándose en las innovaciones de infraestructura y arquitectura para sistemas autónomos.
key_takeaways: Debate sobre el Internet of Cognition con Vijoy Pandey de Cisco.
Análisis de la alineación semántica, scope, Accord y Concord.
Exploración de protocolos de compartición de contexto para agentes.
highlights: Invitado: Vijoy Pandey, SVP y GM de Outshift by Cisco.
Continuación de la charla de marzo sobre protocolos de agentes de IA.

de.why_it_matters: Die Untersuchung, wie KI-Agenten kooperieren und Kontext austauschen, ist entscheidend für das Verständnis zukünftiger intelligenter Netzwerkprotokolle.

Aufbauend auf seinem Auftritt im März kehrt Vijoy Pandey, SVP und GM von Outshift by Cisco, zurück, um über übergeordnete Protokolle für KI-Agenten zu sprechen. it.title: Agenti AI che collaborano: Cisco discute di Scope, Accord e Concord
it.summary: In questo episodio, Vijoy Pandey di Cisco affronta le sfide dei sistemi multi-agente. Vengono presentati protocolli open-source come Scope, Accord e Concord per coordinare flussi di lavoro autonomi.
it.why_it_matters: I protocolli aperti mirano a risolvere i problemi di coordinamento tra diversi sistemi di intelligenza artificiale, facilitando l'allineamento semantico e la negoziazione degli intenti.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama dell'intelligenza artificiale si sta evolvendo verso ecosistemi in cui più agenti autonomi devono operare congiuntamente. Tuttavia, far comunicare e collaborare questi sistemi presenta notevoli complessità tecniche.

Nel corso dell'episodio, l'approfondimento si concentra su come i protocolli open-source Scope, Accord e Concord cerchino di affrontare tali ostacoli, offrendo un quadro per l'allineamento semantico e la gestione degli intenti nei flussi di lavoro distribuiti.

Gli ascoltatori possono approfondire le dinamiche di progettazione dei sistemi multi-agente e le soluzioni proposte per abilitare una cooperazione efficace tra intelligenze artificiali autonome.
it.context: La discussione si inserisce nel contesto della crescente adozione di agenti intelligenti autonomi e della necessità di standard aperti per evitare ecosistemi frammentati e proprietari.
key_takeaways: Le sfide della collaborazione nei sistemi multi-agente.
Il ruolo dei protocolli open-source Scope, Accord e Concord.
Strategie per l'allineamento semantico e la negoziazione degli intenti.

en.title: AI Agents That Think Together: Cisco's Vijoy Pandey on Multi-Agent Systems
en.summary: Vijoy Pandey of Cisco discusses multi-agent AI challenges and explores how open-source protocols like Scope, Accord, and Concord enable collaboration and semantic alignment across autonomous workflows.
en.why_it_matters: Open protocols are essential for overcoming coordination hurdles between distinct AI systems, enabling seamless intent negotiation and structured collaboration across autonomous workflows.
en.extended_analysis:
As artificial intelligence shifts from standalone models to interconnected multi-agent ecosystems, managing how different systems cooperate becomes a core architectural challenge. Without unified standards, autonomous agents risk operating in silos.

This episode examines how open-source frameworks such as Scope, Accord, and Concord attempt to address semantic alignment and intent negotiation. By establishing shared protocols, these systems aim to foster more reliable cooperation in complex environments.

Listeners will gain insights into the current engineering approaches designed to make multi-agent collaboration practical and scalable for modern technical infrastructures.
en.context: This discussion addresses the broader industry transition toward collaborative autonomous workflows and the growing demand for interoperable standards in AI development.
key_takeaways: Key challenges in scaling multi-agent AI architectures.
Overview of open-source protocols Scope, Accord, and Concord.
Methods for achieving semantic alignment and intent negotiation.
highlights: Featured guest: Vijoy Pandey, SVP and GM of Outshift by Cisco.
Exploration of open-source protocols for autonomous agent workflows.

es.title: Agentes de IA que colaboran: Cisco analiza alineación semántica y protocolos
es.summary: Vijoy Pandey de Cisco analiza los retos de los sistemas multi-agente y explica cómo protocolos abiertos como Scope, Accord y Concord facilitan la colaboración en flujos de trabajo autónomos.
es.why_it_matters: Los protocolos abiertos buscan resolver los problemas de coordinación entre inteligencias artificiales, mejorando la negociación de intenciones y la alineación semántica.
es.extended_analysis:
A medida que la inteligencia artificial evoluciona hacia arquitecturas multi-agente, la capacidad de distintos sistemas autónomos para cooperar de forma fluida se vuelve crucial. La falta de estándares comunes puede limitar la interoperabilidad.

En este episodio se examinan las propuestas técnicas que utilizan protocolos abiertos como Scope, Accord y Concord para estructurar la colaboración y el alineamiento semántico entre flujos de trabajo automatizados.

Los oyentes pueden conocer las perspectivas de la industria sobre cómo abordar la complejidad operativa de los agentes de IA distribuidos.
es.context: El debate refleja la atención actual sobre la interoperabilidad y el diseño de protocolos abiertos para gestionar sistemas de IA autónomos a gran escala.
key_takeaways: Retos en la colaboración de sistemas multi-agente.
Uso de protocolos abiertos como Scope, Accord y Concord.
Estrategias para la negociación de intenciones y alineación semántica.
highlights: Invitado: Vijoy Pandey, SVP y GM de Outshift by Cisco.
Enfoque en la colaboración mediante protocolos de código abierto.

zh-CN.title: 协同工作的AI代理：思科探讨多智能体系统与开放协议
zh-CN.summary: 思科的Vijoy Pandey探讨了多智能体AI系统的挑战，并介绍了Scope、Accord和Concord等开源协议如何实现自主工作流中的协作与语义对齐。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 开放协议旨在解决不同AI系统之间的协作难题，为自主工作流提供有效的意图协商和语义对齐机制。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能从单一模型向多智能体生态系统演进，如何让不同的自主系统有效协同工作成为了技术架构的关键核心。缺乏统一标准可能导致系统间难以顺畅沟通。

本期节目讨论了Scope、Accord和Concord等开源框架，分析它们如何通过共享协议来应对语义对齐与意图协商的复杂性。

听众可以从中了解当前工程界为实现多智能体协作所进行的探索与实践方向。
zh-CN.context: 本次讨论反映了行业向自主多智能体工作流转型的趋势，以及对构建互操作标准的需求。
key_takeaways: 多智能体AI系统面临的核心挑战。
Scope、Accord和Concord开源协议的作用。
实现语义对齐与意图协商的技术路径。
highlights: 特邀嘉宾：思科Outshift高级副总裁兼总经理Vijoy Pandey。
探讨用于自主工作流的开源协作协议。

de.title: Kooperierende KI-Agenten: Cisco über semantische Ausrichtung und Protokolle
de.summary: Vijoy Pandey von Cisco erörtert die Herausforderungen von Multi-Agenten-Systemen und erklärt, wie offene Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord die Zusammenarbeit in autonomen Arbeitsabläufen ermöglichen.
de.why_it_matters: Offene Protokolle adressieren Koordinationsprobleme zwischen verschiedenen KI-Systemen und erleichtern die semantische Ausrichtung sowie die Intentionsaushandlung.
de.extended_analysis:
Der Übergang zu verteilten Multi-Agenten-Systemen stellt die Softwarearchitektur vor neue Herausforderungen, da autonome KI-Einheiten verlässlich miteinander kommunizieren und kooperieren müssen.

In dieser Episode wird beleuchtet, wie Open-Source-Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord dazu beitragen können, semantische Konsistenz und strukturierte Intentionsaushandlung in komplexen Workflows zu gewährleisten.

Hörer erhalten Einblicke in aktuelle architektonische Lösungsansätze zur Bewältigung der Interoperabilität zwischen autonomen Agenten.
de.context: Die Diskussion spiegelt die technische Entwicklung hin zu vernetzten, autonomen KI-Workflows und den Bedarf an standardisierten Kommunikationsprotokollen wider.
key_takeaways: Herausforderungen bei der Skalierung von Multi-Agenten-Architekturen.
Bedeutung offener Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord.
Ansätze für semantische Ausrichtung und Intentionsaushandlung.
highlights: Gast: Vijoy Pandey, SVP und GM von Outshift by Cisco.
Fokus auf Open-Source-Protokolle für autonome Agenten-Workflows.

it.title: ChatGPT Plus gratuito per oltre 20.000 veterani e militari
it.summary: Oltre 20.000 veterani e militari in transizione hanno ottenuto un anno gratuito di ChatGPT Plus. L'iniziativa mostra come questi utenti sfruttino lo strumento per prepararsi alle carriere civili.
it.why_it_matters: L'adozione di strumenti avanzati di intelligenza artificiale da parte di un numero così elevato di veterani evidenzia il loro utilizzo pratico per la transizione professionale e lavorativa.

it.title: Progettare per gli agenti AI: la prospettiva di Zeno Rocha su Resend
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, Zeno Rocha, fondatore e CEO di Resend, racconta come i coding agent scelgano autonomamente i servizi analizzando i flussi di lavoro. Attraverso il caso in cui un agente ha scelto Resend per una pull request, l'episodio esplora l'ottimizzazione per i motori di risposta.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come gli agenti autonomi prendano decisioni tecniche al posto degli sviluppatori ridefinisce le strategie di visibilità e adozione dei prodotti software.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama dello sviluppo software sta cambiando rapidamente con l'introduzione di agenti di codifica autonomi capaci di compiere scelte tecniche in autonomia, come l'integrazione di servizi di posta elettronica. Zeno Rocha offre una prospettiva privilegiata su questo fenomeno, analizzando cosa significhi trovarsi dal lato ricevente di una raccomandazione generata da un'intelligenza artificiale.

L'episodio approfondisce il concetto di answer engine optimization (AEO) e il suo impatto sulle aziende tecnologiche. Quando i software non si rivolgono più solo agli utenti umani ma dialogano direttamente con gli agenti, le dinamiche di mercato e di branding subiscono una trasformazione radicale.
it.context: La discussione si inserisce nel contesto dell'evoluzione degli strumenti di intelligenza artificiale per gli sviluppatori, dove gli agenti autonomi passano dall'essere semplici assistenti a veri e propri decisori operativi nei flussi di lavoro.
key_takeaways: I coding agent possono scegliere autonomamente i servizi software durante la scrittura del codice.
Zeno Rocha spiega l'ottimizzazione per i motori di risposta (AEO) dal punto di vista di un'azienda.
Il ruolo degli strumenti di sviluppo si sposta dall'interazione umana a quella guidata dagli agenti.

en.title: Designing for Agents: Zeno Rocha on Resend and Autonomous Software

The intersection of autonomous agents and developer tooling is creating new paradigms for how software is adopted. When swyx connected Cloudflare email and a coding agent subsequently opened a pull request selecting Resend, it highlighted a shift in how technical products gain traction.

Zeno Rocha breaks down the mechanics of this shift, discussing answer engine optimization (AEO) and what it means for infrastructure companies when AI agents become the primary decision-makers. This episode offers a look into the future where software is built for both human developers and autonomous coding systems.
en.context: The episode reflects the growing trend of AI coding agents executing complex workflows and making automated architectural decisions on behalf of developers.
key_takeaways: Coding agents can independently select backend services based on project context.
Answer engine optimization (AEO) redefines how developer tools gain visibility.

items.summary: Hello, and welcome back to The Cognitive Revolution. Today, my guest is Curt Tigges, member of technical staff at Goodfire, and with Nick Cammarata, co-author of the new paper, "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis," the more academic and more LLM-focused companion to Nick's recent

it.title: Decodificare i modelli linguistici: Curt Tigges su interpretabilità e basis
it.summary: In questo episodio di The Cognitive Revolution, il conduttore esplora con Curt Tigges di Goodfire la ricerca sul paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". L'intervista approfondisce l'interpretabilità agentica, la monosemanticità e il reverse engineering dei modelli.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come i singoli neuroni e le basi interpretabili operino all'interno dei grandi modelli linguistici è cruciale per demistificare il loro funzionamento interno e avanzare verso sistemi più trasparenti.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio vede come ospite Curt Tigges, membro dello staff tecnico di Goodfire e coautore insieme a Nick Cammarata del nuovo paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". La discussione si muove attorno ai concetti chiave di interpretabilità agentica, monosemanticità e reverse engineering dei sistemi di intelligenza artificiale. items.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our new models for the hardest technical challenges. Fable 5.2 sets a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences.
items.sourceEvidence: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our new models for the hardest technical challenges. Fable 5.2 sets a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences. Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude Introduction Performance and efficiency Coding Cybersecurity Science and engineering Safety and alignment Data privacy Availability November 9, 2026 Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 [1] Introduction [2] Performance and efficiency [3] Science and engineering [4] Safety and alignment [5] Availability We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below. Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users. Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs. Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models. They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also come with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. Fast mode is available for $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. Safety and alignment. To help ensure safety and alignment keep step with growing model capabilities, we ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes. We believe high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1 but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks. We describe more about our safety testing below, and full details can be found in the Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 System Card . When to use Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Fable and Mythos are best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work. For most coding and knowledge tasks, we recommend that users start with Claude Opus 5.5, our strongest daily driver, and then switch to a different model as required, depending on the scope and complexity of their work—upward to Fable or Mythos, or downward to Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5. Fable 5.2 can also play the role of Advisor (where Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus models consult it to help solve harder problems) or Orchestrator (where it delegates simpler tasks to smaller models). Evaluating Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Benchmark performance. The benchmarks table below shows that Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are a step above Opus 5.5 in almost all the capabilities we evaluated: Fable 5.2 Fable 5.1 Opus 5.5 GPT-6 Astra Gemini 4 Carbon Agentic coding FrontierCode 2.0 Agentic coding FrontierCode 2.0 49.1% Xhigh effort 32.4% Xhigh effort 45.5% 42.8% 41.1% Medium effort Agentic coding FrontierSWE v2 Agentic coding FrontierSWE v2 69.9% 56.3% 62.3% 65.5% 61.2% Business workflows AutomationBench Business workflows AutomationBench 51.4% 31.4% 42.5% 41.4% 53.9% Agentic scientific research Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 Agentic scientific research Terminal-Bench-S

items.title: Canva Is Tackling AI Design’s Most Frustrating Problem with Stefano Corazza- #784
items.summary: In this episode, Stefano Corazza, head of AI research at Canva, joins us to explore how his team is building custom models and agents around iterative design workflows. We discuss the tradeoffs between training models from scratch and adapting open weights models, and how proprietary design data supports specialization. Stefano explains how Craft separates layout planning from pixel generation and how Brush uses design tools and visual feedback to create and revise compositions. We examine the challenges of evaluating design quality beyond a single generation, including the use of vision language models as judges alongside human evaluation. We also discuss lessons from simplifying agent harnesses, why faster inference enables more iterations, and how model ownership creates opportunities to optimize serving costs. Finally, we explore how APIs and MCP are expanding access to these capabilities and what changes when software companies build tools for agents as well as people. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠⁠https://twimlai.com/go/784.

items.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 pays close attention to who owns the code it works on. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model tended to add to the existing structure when the prompt said nothing about ownership or presented the code base as someone else’s, even when that duplicated existing code. When the prompt said the code base was the model’s own, it often consolidated duplicated code and sometimes made related fixes without being asked. If you want the model to improve the structure as it works, say that the code is its own: You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. The ownership sentence makes the model much more likely to consolidate duplicated code into one shared function. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model consolidated duplicated code in under 10 percent of runs without the sentence and in about 75 percent of runs with it. — Prompting Claude Fable 5.2 , Anthropic documentation Tags: prompt-engineering , anthropic , generative-ai , ai , llms , claude-mythos-fable

You can see them all here - here's the best result I got, from xhigh : max failed to return an image at all, running out of tokens after spending 128,000 thinking about them . That's the same bug that I saw with Opus 5.5 - but it's new for the Fable series, both Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 returned max effort pelicans just fine. items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.summary: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn't want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator , a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room. Here's what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while: You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners - I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra. The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn't work particularly well, so I added a "Rough mode" where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds. Once that's set up, the devices all listen for the beep! I added a clapping mode too so I could test it by clapping my hands in different locations around the room - displayed as diamonds on the map. This helped me gain confidence that it was capable of locating a sound. Beeps show up on the map as an X, plus a line in the "Sounds located" log. You can replay these sounds (from each device in turn) to confirm they are the mysterious beep you are looking for, then click "This is the mystery beep" to mark them as such. (98KB) They aren't identical - you can see what Claude said about that in the transcript (I don't fully understand why it differed): https://claude.ai/share/e56d163e-2793-4677-aa11-191d5058b414 But yeah, it turns out Claude Opus 5.5 is perfectly capable of 3D modeling in Vanilla JS + WebGL without Three.js. items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
items.summary: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. They're too good at describing the work The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb. It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention. I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right. Hide most of it in a details/summary The HTML <details><summary> elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this: < details > < summary > Claude Opus 5.5 </ summary > < h2 > The hook </ h2 > Plugins implement < code > register_agent_reference_types(datasette) </ code > ... </ details > When rendered, it looks like this : Crucially, <details><summary> is supported in GitHub Mar

it.title: Come Stanford insegna l'ingegneria basata sull'IA con Mihail Eric
it.summary: In un'epoca in cui un agente di codifica può completare i compiti dello scorso anno con un solo prompt, come si evolve la didattica? Questo episodio speciale di Latent Space esplora la seconda edizione del corso CS146S di Stanford insieme a Mihail Eric.
it.why_it_matters: Ridefinisce la formazione tecnica quando gli strumenti di IA automatizzano la programmazione di base, spingendo gli studenti ad affrontare repository open-source complessi e a proporre modifiche reali.
it.extended_analysis:
Con la diffusione di agenti di codifica capaci di svolgere i vecchi compiti scolastici in un solo passaggio, la didattica universitaria deve reinventarsi. Nel secondo ciclo del corso CS146S di Stanford, l'approccio educativo si sposta verso sfide reali, come l'integrazione di manutentori open-source all'interno del percorso accademico.

Gli studenti si trovano così a dover esplorare codebase a loro sconosciute, comprendere logiche altrui e proporre modifiche concrete. Questo episodio speciale offre una prospettiva su come preparare la prossima generazione di ingegneri a un panorama tecnologico radicalmente trasformato dall'intelligenza artificiale.
it.context: Il panorama dello sviluppo software sta cambiando rapidamente grazie agli strumenti di intelligenza artificiale generativa per il codice, costringendo le università a ripensare i metodi di insegnamento tradizionali.
key_takeaways: Esame della seconda edizione del corso CS146S all'Università di Stanford.
Coinvolgimento diretto di manutentori open-source all'interno del percorso didattico.
Nuovi metodi d'insegnamento per affrontare l'era degli agenti di codifica automatizzati.

en.title: How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering with Mihail Eric
en.summary: When a coding agent can finish last year's homework in a single prompt, how does education adapt? This special episode of Latent Space examines the second run of Stanford's CS146S course with guest Mihail Eric.
en.why_it_matters: It highlights how computer science education is shifting as AI automates routine coding, forcing students to tackle unfamiliar open-source repositories and propose real changes.
en.extended_analysis:
As coding agents become capable of completing legacy coursework in a single prompt, technical education faces an urgent need for reinvention. In the second iteration of Stanford's CS146S course, the curriculum brings open-source maintainers directly into the classroom experience.

Students are challenged to navigate unfamiliar codebases, understand complex architectures, and propose substantive changes. This special episode provides a window into how academic institutions are adapting their teaching models for an AI-native engineering workforce.
en.context: The rise of advanced coding agents has disrupted traditional computer science assignments, prompting top universities to redesign their curricula around real-world software maintenance and collaboration.
key_takeaways: Insights into the second run of Stanford's CS146S course.
The integration of open-source maintainers into the student learning process.
Educational strategies for a world where coding agents handle routine assignments.

es.extended_analysis:
Con la llegada de agentes capaces de resolver tareas antiguas en una sola instrucción, las universidades deben replantearse sus métodos. En la segunda entrega del curso CS146S de Stanford, se introducen mantenedores de código abierto directamente en la dinámica del curso.

Los alumnos deben aprender a desenvolverse en repositorios ajenos y proponer modificaciones reales. Este episodio ofrece una perspectiva sobre cómo se forma a los futuros ingenieros en la era de la inteligencia artificial.
es.context: La irrupción de la IA en el desarrollo de software está transformando los métodos pedagógicos tradicionales en las principales instituciones académicas.
key_takeaways: Revisión de la segunda edición del curso CS146S de Stanford.
Colaboración con mantenedores de proyectos de código abierto en el ámbito académico.
Nuevos enfoques educativos ante la automatización de tareas de programación.

Discusión sobre el impacto de los agentes de programación en la enseñanza.

de.title: Wie Stanford KI-native Softwaretechnik lehrt mit Mihail Eric
de.summary: Wenn ein Programmierassistent die Hausaufgaben des Vorjahres mit einem einzigen Prompt erledigt, wie passt sich die Lehre an? Diese Sonderfolge von Latent Space beleuchtet die zweite Auflage von Stanfords CS146S-Kurs mit Mihail Eric.
de.why_it_matters: Es zeigt, wie sich die technische Ausbildung wandelt, während KI routinehafte Programmierarbeiten automatisiert und Studenten vor die Aufgabe stellt, fremde Open-Source-Repositories zu bearbeiten.
de.extended_analysis:
Da Code-Agenten in der Lage sind, klassische Programmieraufgaben in einem einzigen Durchgang zu lösen, steht die technische Ausbildung vor einer grundlegenden Neuausrichtung. In der zweiten Runde des Kurses CS146S an der Stanford University wurden Open-Source-Maintainer direkt in den Lehrplan integriert.

Die Studierenden lernen dabei, sich in unbekannte Repositories einzuarbeiten, bestehende Strukturen zu verstehen und konkrete Änderungen vorzuschlagen. Diese Sonderepisode bietet Einblicke in die Anpassung akademischer Lehrmethoden an ein durch künstliche Intelligenz geprägtes Umfeld.
de.context: Der Vormarsch fortschrittlicher Programmier-Agenten stellt traditionelle Aufgabenformate in der Informatik vor neue Herausforderungen und treibt Universitäten dazu an, ihre Lehrpläne anzupassen.

items.title: Can AI Invent or Just Help Scientists Work Faster? with Richard Socher - #783
items.summary: AI can help scientists write code, analyze data, and draft papers. But can it generate the ideas that lead to new discoveries? Richard Socher, former chief scientist at Salesforce, founder of You.com, and co-founder of Recursive, joins us to explore the move from AI assisting researchers to AI conducting research. Starting with AI improving AI, we examine what it takes to propose ideas, run experiments, and validate results, and how those capabilities could eventually accelerate discovery across biology, chemistry, and physics. The conversation covers Recursive’s reported results in model training and GPU kernel optimization, why fast verification matters, and how reward hacking complicates the search for real improvements. We also discuss the data and experimental infrastructure needed for broader scientific discovery, whether commercial incentives can keep increasingly capable systems aligned, and Richard’s vision for a “Eureka machine.” 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠https://twimlai.com/go/783.
items.podcastDescription: Ricerca, machine learning e applicazioni raccontati da ricercatori e professionisti.

it.title: L'IA può inventare o solo aiutare gli scienziati? Con Richard Socher

it.why_it_matters: Comprendere se l'intelligenza artificiale possa generare nuove idee e scoperte scientifiche apre interrogativi cruciali sul futuro della ricerca in biologia, chimica e fisica.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio esamina il passaggio dell'IA dal supporto nella scrittura di codice e analisi dati alla capacità di proporre idee, eseguire esperimenti e validare risultati. Vengono discussi i risultati riportati da Recursive nell'addestramento dei modelli e nell'ottimizzazione dei kernel GPU, oltre ai problemi legati al reward hacking.

La conversazione affronta inoltre l'infrastruttura di dati ed esperimenti necessaria per la scoperta scientifica, gli incentivi commerciali per l'allineamento dei sistemi e la visione di Richard Socher di una "macchina di Eureka".
it.context: Il dibattito si inserisce nel contesto della transizione tecnologica in cui i modelli di IA avanzano verso compiti di ragionamento e automazione scientifica complessa.
key_takeaways: Il passaggio dell'IA da assistente a conduttrice di ricerca.
L'importanza della verifica rapida e le complicazioni del reward hacking.
La visione di una 'macchina di Eureka' per accelerare le scoperte.

en.extended_analysis:
The episode examines AI moving from code writing and data analysis support to proposing ideas, running experiments, and validating results. It covers Recursive's reported results in model training and GPU kernel optimization, alongside the challenges of reward hacking.

The conversation also explores the data and experimental infrastructure required for scientific discovery, commercial alignment incentives, and Richard's vision for a "Eureka machine."
en.context: This discussion addresses the broader technological transition as advanced AI systems edge closer to autonomous scientific reasoning and execution.
key_takeaways: The evolution of AI from research assistant to active researcher.
The role of fast verification and the complications introduced by reward hacking.
Infrastructure and incentives needed for broader scientific discovery.

it.why_it_matters: Affrontare la privacy e la riservatezza dei dati è una delle sfide cruciali nello sviluppo di strumenti di intelligenza artificiale per settori regolamentati come quello legale.

Lo sviluppo di agenti autonomi in contesti ad alta sensibilità informativa richiede soluzioni architetturali innovative per garantire la totale riservatezza. Poiché i dati appartengono ai clienti dello studio legale, i progettisti devono trovare metodi rigorosi per verificare le prestazioni senza violare il segreto professionale o accedere ai contenuti operativi.

L'intervista con Jacob Lauritzen offre uno sguardo approfondito sulle metodologie ingegneristiche adottate da una delle aziende a maggiore crescita nel settore, evidenziando il bilanciamento tra automazione avanzata e rigidi vincoli di sicurezza dei dati.

it.title: Perché gli agenti IA amano Supabase
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, i cofondatori di Supabase Paul Copplestone e Ant Wilson discutono con swyx di come la programmazione guidata dagli agenti IA stia trasformando le esigenze dei database e dei backend.
it.why_it_matters: La crescente diffusione di software creato da agenti IA impone nuove sfide e funzionalità ai backend, come la gestione di carichi di lavoro a lungo termine e schemi più comprensibili.
it.extended_analysis:
Man mano che gli agenti IA assumono ruoli di rilievo nella creazione di software, le infrastrutture tradizionali devono adattarsi. La conversazione esplora le modifiche necessarie per consentire agli agenti di interagire in modo efficiente con i dati e i carichi di lavoro.

Vengono esaminate le soluzioni per affiancare carichi di lavoro persistenti direttamente al database e semplificare la struttura dei dati affinché i sistemi autonomi possano interpretarli senza ostacoli.

Nel contesto attuale dell'ingegneria del software, comprendere l'evoluzione dei backend orientati agli agenti è fondamentale per anticipare le tendenze dello sviluppo tecnologico.
it.context: L'episodio si inserisce nel dibattito in evoluzione sull'adattamento delle infrastrutture dati tradizionali alle nuove esigenze imposte dall'automazione avanzata e dalla generazione di codice tramite intelligenza artificiale.
key_takeaways: I carichi di lavoro a lungo termine richiedono nuove strategie di gestione accanto al database.
Gli schemi semplificati aiutano gli agenti IA a comprendere e scrivere software in modo efficace.

items.summary: AI agents are becoming accessible to everyone, raising the bar for developers building the next generation of agent products. When capable, general-purpose agents are available out of the box, differentiation increasingly comes down to the architectural decisions and specialized experiences that make an agent uniquely valuable. it.title: Sviluppo di exploit, agenti IA e PoC falsi nella cybersecurity
it.summary: In questo episodio di Practical AI, Daniel e Chris discutono con Spencer McIntyre di VulnCheck su come l'intelligenza artificiale stia accelerando la ricerca di vulnerabilità e lo sviluppo di exploit, affrontando anche il problema dei PoC inaffidabili.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere l'impatto dell'IA sulla sicurezza informatica aiuta a distinguere le reali minacce dai falsi allarmi, migliorando le strategie di difesa e intelligence.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama della sicurezza informatica sta affrontando trasformazioni significative grazie all'uso di agenti IA per la scoperta di vulnerabilità e lo sviluppo di exploit. Durante l'episodio, gli ospiti analizzano le sfide legate all'affidabilità dei proof-of-concept (PoC) e i limiti delle barriere di sicurezza (guardrails) per i ricercatori.

Vengono inoltre esaminate le soluzioni di intelligence per l'accesso iniziale, utili ai team di sicurezza per dare priorità alle minacce concrete, offrendo uno sguardo sulle prospettive future della threat intelligence.
it.context: L'episodio esplora l'intersezione tra intelligenza artificiale e cybersecurity, evidenziando le nuove opportunità e i rischi associati all'automazione della ricerca sulle vulnerabilità.
key_takeaways: L'IA accelera la ricerca di vulnerabilità e lo sviluppo di exploit.
Molti proof-of-concept (PoC) generati presentano limiti di affidabilità.
L'intelligence sull'accesso iniziale aiuta i team a prioritizzare le minacce reali.
highlights: Intervista a Spencer McIntyre, Direttore dello Sviluppo Exploit presso VulnCheck.
Discussione sui limiti dei guardrail dell'IA per i ricercatori di sicurezza.

en.title: Exploit Development, Agentic Vulnerability Discovery, and Fake PoCs

In this episode, the hosts and guest explore the utilization of agents for discovering security flaws and address the phenomenon where numerous proof-of-concept exploits fail to deliver functional results.

The conversation also covers the constraints of AI guardrails affecting security researchers and the role of initial access intelligence in helping teams focus on genuine threats within modern threat landscapes.
en.context: The discussion reflects the broader industry dialogue regarding the integration of automated agents into offensive and defensive cybersecurity workflows.
key_takeaways: AI is accelerating both vulnerability research and exploit development.
Many proof-of-concept exploits face significant reliability and execution issues.
Initial access intelligence supports security teams in prioritizing actual threats.

es.context: El episodio aborda el contexto actual donde la automatización y los agentes autónomos influyen en las operaciones de seguridad ofensiva y defensiva.
key_takeaways: La IA acelera la investigación de vulnerabilidades y el desarrollo de exploits.
Muchos exploits de prueba (PoCs) presentan problemas de eficacia.
La inteligencia de acceso inicial ayuda a priorizar amenazas reales.

Discusión sobre los desafíos de los guardarraíles de la IA para investigadores.

items.title: Airbnb Is Building a ‘Company Brain’ for AI Agents with Ahmad Al-Dahle - #781
items.summary: AI agents need the institutional knowledge experienced employees rely on: why a system works a certain way, which policies apply, and what never made it into the documentation. Capturing that knowledge is hard. Keeping it useful as people and agents add more may be harder. In this episode, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, shares how his team is building Project Everest, a “company brain” that captures knowledge from employees’ workflows for AI agents. We explore stale information and context poisoning, why too much context can backfire, and how the team evaluates whether shared knowledge improves engineering work. We also discuss measuring AI productivity beyond token usage and PR counts, the limits of chat-based interfaces, and deploying support agents in a marketplace where resolving disputes means mediating between conflicting interests. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/781.

it.title: Airbnb e il 'cervello aziendale' per gli agenti IA
it.summary: In questo episodio, Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO di Airbnb, illustra Project Everest, un sistema progettato per catturare la conoscenza istituzionale dai flussi di lavoro dei dipendenti e metterla a disposizione degli agenti IA. L'episodio approfondisce le sfide legate alla gestione delle informazioni obsolete e del contesto in eccesso.
it.why_it_matters: Catturare la conoscenza non documentata è cruciale per permettere agli agenti IA di operare efficacemente in contesti aziendali complessi, evitando problemi legati all'affidabilità delle informazioni.
it.extended_analysis:
Gli agenti IA dipendono spesso dalla conoscenza tacita che i dipendenti esperti accumulano nel tempo, la quale raramente entra a far parte della documentazione ufficiale. Airbnb sta affrontando questa sfida con Project Everest, un'infrastruttura pensata per raccogliere e organizzare tale sapere aziendale.

Durante la conversazione, vengono esaminati i rischi derivanti da informazioni obsolete e dal fenomeno del 'context poisoning', in cui una quantità eccessiva o scorretta di dati può compromettere le prestazioni dei sistemi intelligenti. Vengono inoltre analizzati i metodi per valutare l'impatto reale del lavoro ingegneristico e le limitazioni delle interfacce basate su chat.
it.context: Nel panorama tecnologico attuale, le aziende cercano di andare oltre i semplici assistenti conversazionali, puntando su agenti autonomi capaci di integrarsi nei processi operativi quotidiani e di mediare in scenari complessi.
key_takeaways: Project Everest raccoglie la conoscenza aziendale nascosta nei flussi di lavoro per gli agenti IA.
Il 'context poisoning' e la gestione di informazioni obsolete rappresentano ostacoli significativi.
La misurazione della produttività dell'IA richiede metriche che vanno oltre i token o il conteggio delle PR.
highlights: Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO di Airbnb, è ospite dell'episodio.
Si discute dell'impiego di agenti di supporto in un mercato basato sulla mediazione di dispute.

en.title: Airbnb's Company Brain for AI Agents with Ahmad Al-Dahle
en.summary: In this episode, Airbnb CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle discusses Project Everest, a system designed to capture institutional knowledge from employee workflows for AI agents. The conversation explores stale information, context poisoning, and evaluating shared knowledge in engineering.
en.why_it_matters: Equipping AI agents with institutional knowledge is essential for effective deployment, yet capturing and maintaining accurate context remains a major technical challenge.
en.extended_analysis:
AI agents frequently lack the unwritten institutional knowledge that experienced employees rely on daily, from policy nuances to undocumented system behaviors. Airbnb's Project Everest aims to bridge this gap by capturing workflow insights directly from staff.

The discussion covers the complexities of maintaining relevance, avoiding context poisoning where excess data backfires, and evaluating whether shared knowledge genuinely enhances engineering output. Additional topics include measuring AI productivity beyond simplistic metrics and deploying marketplace support agents.
en.context: As organizations shift from basic chat assistants to autonomous AI agents, providing reliable internal data and managing information overload have become critical bottlenecks.
key_takeaways: Project Everest serves as a 'company brain' to supply AI agents with workflow knowledge.
Managing stale information and context overload prevents system backfires.
Evaluating AI productivity requires moving beyond traditional metrics like token usage and PR counts.
highlights: Ahmad Al-Dahle, CTO of Airbnb, shares insights on building internal AI systems.

es.why_it_matters: Dotar a los agentes de IA de conocimientos no documentados es clave para su éxito operativo, pero mantener la información útil y actualizada plantea grandes retos.
es.extended_analysis:
Los agentes de IA necesitan comprender los matices internos y las políticas que los empleados experimentados conocen de forma intuitiva. Para resolverlo, Airbnb ha desarrollado Project Everest, un sistema destinado a capturar el conocimiento directamente de las tareas cotidianas.

El debate aborda los riesgos del exceso de contexto y la información desactualizada, así como las formas de evaluar si el conocimiento compartido mejora el trabajo de ingeniería. También se discuten los límites de las interfaces de chat y la implementación de agentes de soporte en mercados complejos.
es.context: La transición hacia agentes de IA autónomos en entornos empresariales exige resolver cómo las máquinas procesan y validan la información interna sin perder precisión.
key_takeaways: Project Everest captura el conocimiento de los flujos de trabajo para alimentar a los agentes de IA.
El exceso de contexto y la información obsoleta pueden reducir la eficacia del sistema.
Se exploran formas avanzadas de medir la productividad de la IA más allá de las métricas básicas.

zh-CN.why_it_matters: 为 AI 代理提供未公开的机构知识对于其有效运作至关重要，但如何捕捉并维护准确的上下文仍然是一项重大的技术挑战。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
AI 代理通常缺乏经验丰富的员工所依赖的隐性机构知识，例如政策细微差别和未文档化的系统行为。爱彼迎的 Project Everest 旨在通过直接从员工的工作流程中收集见解来弥补这一差距。

讨论还涉及维护相关性的复杂性、避免因数据过多而适得其反的“上下文污染”，以及评估共享知识是否真正提升了工程产出。其他议题包括超越传统指标来衡量 AI 生产力，以及在市场环境中部署支持代理。
zh-CN.context: 随着企业从基础聊天助手向自主 AI 代理转型，提供可靠的内部数据并管理信息过载已成为关键瓶颈。
key_takeaways: Project Everest 作为“公司大脑”，为 AI 代理提供工作流程知识。
管理过时信息和上下文过载可防止系统产生负面效果。
评估 AI 生产力需要超越代数使用量和 PR 计数等传统指标。
highlights: 爱彼迎 CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle 分享了构建内部 AI 系统的见解。
节目探讨了在涉及各方利益冲突的市场中使用自动化支持代理进行争议调解。

de.title: Airbnbs Firmengehirn für KI-Agenten mit Ahmad Al-Dahle
de.summary: In dieser Episode bespricht Airbnb-CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle Project Everest, ein System zur Erfassung institutioneller Wissensbestände aus Mitarbeiter-Workflows für KI-Agenten. Themen sind Veraltung, Kontext-Vergiftung und die Evaluierung geteilten Wissens.
de.why_it_matters: KI-Agenten mit implizitem Unternehmenswissen auszustatten ist entscheidend für den Praxiseinsatz, doch die Pflege akkurater Kontexte stellt Entwickler vor enorme Herausforderungen.
de.extended_analysis:
KI-Agenten verfügen oft nicht über das unausgesprochene institutionelle Wissen erfahrener Mitarbeiter, wie Richtliniennuancen oder undokumentierte Systemabläufe. Airbnbs Project Everest soll diese Lücke schließen, indem Workflow-Erkenntnisse direkt erfasst werden.

Die Diskussion beleuchtet die Komplexität bei der Vermeidung veralteter Informationen und von 'Context Poisoning', bei dem überschüssige Daten die Leistung verschlechtern. Zudem werden die Messung echter KI-Produktivität jenseits einfacher Metriken sowie der Einsatz von Support-Agenten in umstrittenen Marktplatz-Szenarien erörtert.
de.context: Während Unternehmen von einfachen Chat-Assistenten zu autonomen KI-Agenten übergehen, entwickelt sich die Bereitstellung verlässlicher interner Daten zu einem zentralen Engpass.
key_takeaways: Project Everest dient als Firmengehirn zur Bereitstellung von Workflow-Wissen für KI-Agenten.
Die Handhabung veralteter Informationen verhindert negative Systemrückkopplungen.
Die Messung der KI-Produktivität erfordert Metriken jenseits von Token-Nutzung und Pull Requests.
highlights: Airbnb-CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle ist zu Gast in der Episode.
Es wird der Einsatz von Support-Agenten zur Vermittlung in Marktplatz-Streitigkeiten diskutiert.
