items.title: Why the Next AI Breakthrough May Come from Physics with Max Welling - #774
items.summary: The conventional wisdom in AI is that the next breakthrough will come from more compute, more data, and larger models. But what if the next leap comes from somewhere else? In this episode, Max Welling—co-founder and CTO of CuspAI and professor at the University of Amsterdam—argues that physics may provide some of the ideas behind the next generation of AI systems. We begin with CuspAI’s work using generative AI to design entirely new materials for semiconductors, batteries, carbon capture, and clean energy. Max explains how foundation models for chemistry, agentic workflows, simulation, and automated experimentation are dramatically accelerating the search for new materials and reshaping scientific discovery. The conversation then broadens into a deeper question. Beyond giving AI new scientific problems to solve, can physics also teach us how to build better AI? Max explores surprising connections between machine learning and thermodynamics, why waves may become a new computational primitive for neural networks, and how concepts like symmetry breaking and statistical physics could inspire AI architectures beyond today’s scaling paradigm. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/774.
items.podcastDescription: Ricerca, machine learning e applicazioni raccontati da ricercatori e professionisti.

it.title: Il prossimo grande balzo dell'IA arriverà dalla fisica?
it.summary: In questo episodio, Max Welling esplora come la fisica potrebbe ispirare la prossima generazione di sistemi di intelligenza artificiale, andando oltre il paradigma di scalatura basato solo su dati e calcolo. L'episodio approfondisce l'uso dell'IA generativa per la progettazione di nuovi materiali e i legami tra apprendimento automatico e termodinamica.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere se la fisica possa offrire nuove architetture per l'IA è fondamentale per superare gli attuali limiti di efficienza e scalabilità dei modelli.
it.extended_analysis:
La saggezza convenzionale nell'IA punta su sempre più dati e potenza di calcolo, ma alternative come la fisica statistica e la simmetria potrebbero sbloccare nuove direzioni. Max Welling, co-fondatore e CTO di CuspAI e professore all'Università di Amsterdam, discute come i modelli di fondazione per la chimica e i flussi di lavoro agentici stiano accelerando la scoperta scientifica.

L'analisi si sposta poi su connessioni sorprendenti, come l'uso delle onde come primitive computazionali e il ruolo della termodinamica. Questi concetti offrono una prospettiva stimolante su come potremmo concepire le future architetture di rete.

Restano da monitorare gli sviluppi pratici di queste idee teoriche e la loro effettiva integrazione nei sistemi di produzione commerciale.
it.context: Il dibattito sulla ricerca di nuovi paradigmi oltre il semplice aumento dei parametri riflette la necessità di rendere l'IA più efficiente e radicata nei principi scientifici fondamentali.
key_takeaways: La fisica potrebbe ispirare le future architetture di IA oltre il modello di scalatura attuale.
L'IA generativa accelera la scoperta di materiali per semiconduttori, batterie e cattura del carbonio.
Concetti come onde, termodinamica e rottura di simmetria offrono nuove primitive computazionali.
highlights: Ospite: Max Welling, co-fondatore e CTO di CuspAI e professore all'Università di Amsterdam.

en.title: Will the Next AI Breakthrough Come from Physics?
en.summary: In this episode, Max Welling discusses how physics may provide ideas for the next generation of AI systems, challenging the conventional wisdom of scaling compute and data alone. The conversation covers CuspAI's work in designing new materials and explores unexpected connections between machine learning and thermodynamics.
en.why_it_matters: Exploring physics-inspired architectures could offer a vital alternative to overcome the limitations of current compute-heavy scaling paradigms.
en.extended_analysis:
While conventional AI progress relies heavily on larger models and more data, alternative avenues rooted in foundational sciences deserve scrutiny. Max Welling, co-founder and CTO of CuspAI and professor at the University of Amsterdam, outlines how generative AI, simulation, and agentic workflows are accelerating scientific discovery for clean energy and semiconductors.

The discussion goes further by examining whether physics can teach us how to build better AI. Welling explores connections between machine learning, statistical physics, waves as computational primitives, and symmetry breaking.

Observers should watch how these theoretical concepts translate into concrete architectural designs for future machine learning systems.
en.context: As scaling laws face physical and economic constraints, researchers are increasingly looking toward fundamental physics for alternative pathways in AI architecture design.
key_takeaways: Physics concepts like thermodynamics and symmetry breaking may inspire future AI architectures.
Generative AI and foundation models for chemistry are rapidly accelerating materials discovery.
Waves could potentially emerge as a new computational primitive for neural networks.
highlights: Guest: Max Welling, co-founder and CTO of CuspAI and professor at the University of Amsterdam.
Exploration of automated experimentation and agentic workflows in scientific discovery.

es.title: ¿El próximo gran avance de la IA vendrá de la física?
es.summary: En este episodio, Max Welling analiza cómo la física podría inspirar la próxima generación de sistemas de inteligencia artificial, más allá de depender únicamente de más datos y potencia de cálculo. La charla explora el diseño de nuevos materiales y las conexiones entre el aprendizaje automático y la termodinámica.
es.why_it_matters: Examinar enfoques basados en la física es clave para superar los límites actuales del paradigma de escalado basado puramente en la fuerza bruta computacional.
es.extended_analysis:
La sabiduría convencional sostiene que el próximo avance de la IA vendrá de más computación, pero Max Welling, cofundador y CTO de CuspAI y profesor en la Universidad de Ámsterdam, argumenta que la física podría aportar ideas fundamentales. La conversación detalla cómo los modelos de IA generativa aceleran la búsqueda de materiales para baterías y energía limpia.

Además, se examina si la física puede enseñarnos a construir una mejor IA mediante conceptos como la termodinámica, la ruptura de simetría y el uso de ondas como primitivas computacionales.

Será relevante observar cómo estas propuestas teóricas influyen en el diseño de futuras arquitecturas de redes neuronales.
es.context: La búsqueda de alternativas al modelo de escalado tradicional refleja los desafíos actuales en la eficiencia y fundamentación teórica del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial.
key_takeaways: La física ofrece conceptos como simetría y termodinámica para inspirar arquitecturas de IA.
Los modelos de fundación para la química aceleran drásticamente la descoberta de materiales.
Las ondas podrían convertirse en una nueva primitiva computacional para las redes neuronales.
highlights: Invitado: Max Welling, cofundador y CTO de CuspAI y profesor de la Universidad de Ámsterdam.
Uso de IA generativa y flujos de trabajo agénticos para el diseño de materiales.

zh-CN.title: 人工智能的下一个突破会来自物理学吗？
zh-CN.summary: 在本期节目中，Max Welling探讨了物理学如何为下一代人工智能系统提供灵感，挑战了仅依靠更多算力和数据的主流观点。节目深入讨论了生成式AI在材料设计中的应用以及机器学习与热力学之间的奇妙联系。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 研究物理学启发的架构为突破当前算力扩展范式的局限性提供了关键的替代思路。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
传统观点认为人工智能的突破源于更大的模型和更多数据，但CuspAI联合创始人兼CTO、阿姆斯特丹大学教授Max Welling认为物理学可能带来新的方向。讨论展示了生成式AI、化学基础模型以及自动化实验如何加速清洁能源和半导体材料的发现。

对话进一步探讨了物理学是否能指导构建更好的AI，涉及统计物理学、对称性破缺以及将波作为神经网络计算原语的概念。

未来需要关注这些理论构想将如何实际转化为下一代机器学习系统的架构设计。
zh-CN.context: 随着规模化定律面临现实限制，研究人员正转向基础物理学，以寻找人工智能架构设计的新途径。
key_takeaways: 热力和对称性破缺等物理概念可能启发未来的AI架构。
化学基础模型与生成式AI显著加速了新材料的研发发现。
波的概念可能成为神经网络的新计算原语。
highlights: 嘉宾：Max Welling，CuspAI联合创始人兼CTO、阿姆斯特丹大学教授。
探讨了自动化实验和智能体工作流在科学发现中的应用。

de.title: Kommt der nächste KI-Durchbruch aus der Physik?
de.summary: In dieser Episode diskutiert Max Welling, wie die Physik Ideen für die nächste Generation von KI-Systemen liefern könnte, jenseits des reinen Skalierungsparadigmas von Rechenleistung und Daten. Die Episode beleuchtet den Einsatz generativer KI für neue Materialien und Verbindungen zur Thermodynamik.
de.why_it_matters: Die Untersuchung physikalischer Ansätze bietet eine entscheidende Perspektive, um die Grenzen aktueller, rechenintensiver Skalierungsmethoden zu überwinden.
de.extended_analysis:
Während der konventionelle Fortschritt in der KI auf mehr Daten und Modelle setzt, argumentiert Max Welling – Mitbegründer und CTO von CuspAI sowie Professor an der Universität Amsterdam –, dass die Physik wertvolle Impulse geben kann. Er erläutert, wie generative KI und Simulationsmodelle die Suche nach neuen Materialien für Halbleiter und Batterien beschleunigen.

Darüber hinaus wird erörtert, ob die Physik uns helfen kann, bessere KI zu bauen. Welling untersucht Verbindungen zwischen maschinellem Lernen, statistischer Physik, Symmetriebrechung und Wellen als rechnerischen Primitiven.

Es bleibt zu beobachten, wie diese theoretischen Konzepte in zukünftige Architekturen einfließen werden.
de.context: Angesichts der Grenzen rein rechenbasierter Skalierungsansätze suchen Forschende zunehmend nach fundamentalen physikalischen Prinzipien für alternative KI-Architekturen.
key_takeaways: Physikalische Konzepte wie Thermodynamik könnten künftige KI-Architekturen inspirieren.
Generative KI und chemische Grundlagenmodelle beschleunigen die Materialforschung massiv.
Wellen könnten als neue Rechenprimitive für neuronale Netze dienen.
highlights: Gast: Max Welling, Mitbegründer und CTO von CuspAI sowie Professor an der Universität Amsterdam.
Diskussion über automatisierte Experimente und agentenbasierte Workflows in der Wissenschaft.

items.title: Statement on the directive to suspend Fable 5 access
items.summary: The US government has issued an export control directive suspending all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by foreign nationals inside or outside the US.
items.sourceEvidence: The US government has issued an export control directive suspending all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by foreign nationals inside or outside the US. Statement on the directive to suspend Fable 5 access \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Published Jun 12, 2026 Category Policy Topics National security Jailbreaks Safeguards Cybersecurity Legal guardrails Access See more... Related articles Models Jun 30, 2026 Redeploying Fable 5 View more The US government, citing national security authorities, has issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the United States, including foreign national Anthropic employees. The net effect of this order is that we must abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all our customers to ensure compliance. Access to all other Anthropic models will not be affected. We received the directive from the government today at 5:21pm (ET). The letter did not provide specific details of its national security concern. Our understanding is that the government believes it has become aware of a method of bypassing, or “jailbreaking” Fable 5. We reviewed a demonstration of this specific technique being used to identify a small number of previously known, minor vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities all appear relatively simple, and we have found that other publicly-available models are able to discover them as well without requiring a bypass. Anthropic’s posture with respect to Fable’s safeguards, as laid out in our launch blog post , is the following: We have instituted strong safeguards that greatly reduce the likelihood that Fable is misused for tasks related to cybersecurity (among others). In fact, our safeguards are so strong that many users have complained that they are overly broad. In the weeks leading up to the launch of Fable, Anthropic worked with the US government, the UK AISI, multiple private third-party organizations and internal teams to red-team Fable’s safeguards for thousands of hours in total. These tests showed that Fable’s safeguards are substantially more effective than those of any previously deployed model. No testers have yet been able to find a universal jailbreak —a jailbreak method that can very broadly bypass the model’s safeguards, unblocking a wide range of cyber capabilities. We suspect that perfect jailbreak resistance is not currently possible for any model provider. Every safeguard used in the industry is vulnerable to non-universal jailbreaks (which can elicit some cyber information in specific circumstances), and it is likely that universal jailbreaks will eventually be found in the future. We stated this clearly when we released Fable 5. Given that perfect jailbreak resistance does not appear to be possible today, Anthropic adopted a defense in depth strategy with Fable 5. We aimed to make jailbreaks either narrow (in the case of non-universal jailbreaks) or very expensive to produce (in the case of universal jailbreaks), and to combine this with thorough monitoring to quickly detect and shut down any successful attacks. This is also why Anthropic has required 30-day retention of customer data with Fable—a policy change that carries real costs for us with customers , but that allows us to research and mitigate jailbreaks. We stand by this defense in depth strategy. It reduces the risks posed by Fable, making them comparable to the risks of existing models already deployed across the industry. We have not even received a disclosure of a concerning non-universal potential jailbreak that led to a harmful result. The potential jailbreaks that have been disclosed to us are either entirely benign responses or are minor findings that provide no Mythos-specific uplift. To date, the government has only given us verbal evidence of a potential narrow, non-universal jailbreak, which essentially consists of asking the model to read a specific codebase and fix any software flaws. items.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
items.summary: Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we’ve made safe for general use.
items.sourceEvidence: Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we’ve made safe for general use. Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude 01 Evaluating Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 01 Evaluating Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 02 Early feedback for Claude Fable 5 03 Claude Fable 5’s new safeguards 04 Claude Mythos 5 and the trusted access program 05 Availability Published Jun 9, 2026 Category Models Topics Claude Opus Safeguards Cybersecurity Access Coding Life sciences See more... Related articles Frontier Red Team Oct 8, 2026 Launching an opt-in vulnerability-finding service for open-source software View more Update Jul 1, 2026 Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5 redeployed Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are now available. View more Jun 12, 2026 Claude Mythos 5 and Fable 5 access unavailable We are suspending access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. We apologize for this disruption to our customers and are working to restore access as soon as possible. View more Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5 : a Mythos-class 1 model that we’ve made safe for general use. Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability, showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas. The longer and more complex the task, the larger Fable 5’s lead over our other models. Releasing a model this capable comes with risks. Without safeguards, Fable 5’s capabilities in areas like cybersecurity could be misused to cause serious damage. We’ve therefore launched the model with safeguards that mean queries on some topics will instead receive a response from our next-most-capable model, Claude Opus 4.8. To release the model both safely and quickly, we’ve tuned these safeguards conservatively—they’ll sometimes catch harmless requests, though they trigger, on average, in less than 5% of sessions. With more capable models arriving in the coming months, we’re working to improve our safeguards and reduce false positives as quickly as we can. For a small group of cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers, we’re also launching Claude Mythos 5 . It’s the same underlying model as Fable 5, but with the safeguards lifted in some areas. 2 Mythos 5 will initially be deployed through Project Glasswing , in collaboration with the US government, as an upgrade to Claude Mythos Preview. It has the strongest cybersecurity capabilities of any model in the world. Soon, we intend to expand access to Mythos 5 through a broader trusted access program. The capabilities of models like Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have the potential to do profound good for the world. We’ve seen the beginnings of this in Project Glasswing, where the models have helped cyber defenders secure critically important software. We’ve also seen it in life sciences research, where the models are positing novel hypotheses and speeding up the development of new therapeutics. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are being offered at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens—less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview. Today’s joint launch is another step towards our goal of bringing advanced AI capabilities to as many users as possible, as quickly and as safely as we can. Evaluating Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 The table below compares the capabilities of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to other leading models. Fable 5 and Mythos 5 can work autonomously for longer than any previous Claude models. Below we discuss how these skills apply to software engineering, and cover the model’s improved capabilities in knowledge work, vision, memory, and life sciences research. Software engineering. During early testing, Stripe reported that Fable 5 compressed months of engineering into days. In a 50-million-line Ruby codebase, the model performed a codebase-wide migration in a day that would otherwise have taken a whole team over two months by hand. Il rilascio congiunto di Fable 5 e Mythos 5 rappresenta un passaggio importante per rendere accessibili capacità di intelligenza artificiale avanzate mantenendo il controllo sui rischi potenziali. Fable 5 adotta salvaguardie conservative che reindirizzano alcune richieste verso modelli meno recenti quando necessario.

items.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8
items.summary: Claude Opus 4.8 brings stronger performance across coding, agentic tasks, and professional work, and the consistency to handle long-running work.
items.sourceEvidence: Claude Opus 4.8 brings stronger performance across coding, agentic tasks, and professional work, and the consistency to handle long-running work. Introducing Claude Opus 4.8 \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude 01 Opus 4.8’s capabilities Introducing Claude Opus 4.8 01 Opus 4.8’s capabilities 02 Collaborating with Opus 4.8 03 Also launching today 04 A note on effort 05 What’s next? 06 Availability Published May 28, 2026 Category Models Topics Claude Opus Claude Code Coding Agents Alignment Claude Developer Platform See more... Related articles Frontier Red Team Jun 18, 2026 Project Fetch: Phase two View more We’re upgrading Claude Opus to a new version: Claude Opus 4.8. It builds on Opus 4.7 with improvements across benchmarks, and is a more effective collaborator. It’s available today for the same price. Opus 4.8 launches alongside several new features. Users on claude.ai now have control over the amount of effort Claude puts into a task. Claude Code has a new “dynamic workflows” feature that allows it to tackle very large-scale problems. And fast mode for Opus 4.8—where the model can work at 2.5× the speed—is now three times cheaper than it was for previous models. Opus 4.8’s capabilities The table below shows how Opus 4.8 compares to its predecessor and to other models on tests of coding, agentic skills, reasoning, and practical knowledge work tasks. More details and a much wider range of capability evaluations are provided in the Claude Opus 4.8 System Card . Collaborating with Opus 4.8 Early testers have found Claude Opus 4.8 to be more reliable and sharper in its judgment when it’s performing agentic tasks. Below are quotes from many of these testers about their experience collaborating with Opus 4.8: “ Claude Opus 4.8 has noticeably better judgment. In Claude Code, it asks the right questions, catches its own mistakes, pushes back when a plan isn’t sound, and builds up confidence around complex, multi-service explorations before making big changes. It’s a great model to build with. ” Tom Pritchard Staff Engineer “ On our Super-Agent benchmark, Claude Opus 4.8 is the only model to complete every case end-to-end, beating prior Opus models and GPT-5.5 at parity on cost. For agent products in translation, deep research, slide-building, and analysis, it delivers powerful reliability. ” Kay Zhu Co-Founder and CTO “ On CursorBench, Claude Opus 4.8 exceeds prior Opus models across every effort level. Tool calling is meaningfully more efficient, using fewer steps for the same intelligence, and it carries end-to-end tasks through. ” Michael Truell Co-Founder and CEO “ Claude Opus 4.8 delivers the highest score recorded on our Legal Agent Benchmark, and is the first model to break 10% overall on the all-pass standard. For substantive legal work, that’s the kind of accuracy lift that translates directly into how much real attorney work our customers can hand off with confidence. ” Niko Grupen Head of Applied Research “ Claude Opus 4.8 feels like a major quality-of-life update over Opus 4.7: faster, easier to collaborate with, and better at carrying context and style direction across a long session. Opus 4.8 is the model I kept trusting for work where voice, taste, and technical execution all have to happen side-by-side. ” Katie Parrott Staff Writer “ Claude Opus 4.8 is the strongest computer-use and browser-agent model we’ve tested, scoring 84% on Online-Mind2Web, which is a meaningful jump over both Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5.
